observation.visible_scene: A foggy night driving view down a wet road. On the right, a traffic signal glows red, with a yield triangle and a blue directional sign mounted below it on a striped post. On the left, a low building is lit by a warm light. In the center distance a bright, blooming white light (oncoming headlights or a fixed lamp) shines through the mist, casting a reflection on the damp pavement. The haze produces strong glare around all light sources.
visible_changes: A white vehicle showing red lights is present at the right edge of the frame in the first two samples and is no longer visible from the third sample onward.

Apart from that right-edge vehicle, the scene is essentially static: the red signal, the central bright light, the building, and the road markings keep the same positions and sizes across all frames, with no discernible camera pan, zoom, or translation.
The intensity and spread of the central light and the surrounding fog fluctuate only slightly frame to frame, consistent with haze and sensor noise rather than object motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the central bright light is an approaching vehicle that later passes or a stationary source, since its apparent size does not change within the excerpt.
The speed and direction of the white vehicle at the right edge, which is only glimpsed briefly before leaving the frame.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the central glare (headlights vs. street lamp) is ambiguous due to the fog.
Minor frame-to-frame brightness variations of the lights may be exposure/fog artifacts rather than real changes.
